manifest_security.title: Application Data Backup Allowed
manifest_security.description: android:allowBackup is true (or not set, defaulting to true). Any user or attacker with USB access can extract the full app data directory using 'adb backup' without root. Set to false or use android:fullBackupOnly with a proper backup rule.

manifest_security.title: Low Minimum SDK Version (8)
manifest_security.description: minSdkVersion=8 targets Android versions that lack modern security controls (full-disk encryption, SELinux enforcement, runtime permissions). Minimum recommended is 21 (Android 5.0).

manifest_security.title: Low Target SDK Version (16)
manifest_security.description: targetSdkVersion=16 opts out of security improvements introduced in Android 9+ (Pie), including default HTTPS enforcement, restricted access to device identifiers, and background restrictions. Target SDK 28 or higher is strongly recommended.

code_findings.title: Reflection-Based Method Invocation
code_findings.description: getDeclaredMethod/getDeclaredField with invoke() can bypass access controls and is commonly used to evade static analysis. Also indicates potential for runtime code manipulation.

code_findings.title: Sensitive Data on External Storage
code_findings.description: Data written to external storage is readable by any app with READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission. Do not store sensitive data on SD card or external volumes.

code_findings.title: Sensitive Data in Log Statement
code_findings.description: Log.d/e/i/v/w() call contains keywords suggesting sensitive data (password, token, key, secret, auth, credential). Log output is accessible to other apps via logcat on unpatched or rooted devices.

code_findings.title: printStackTrace() Leaks Stack Information
code_findings.description: printStackTrace() prints internal class names, method names, and file paths to logcat, aiding reverse engineering and revealing architectural details to attackers.
